lesson.intro: Una oracion escindida (cleft) parte una frase en dos para destacar un elemento y, a menudo, contrastarlo o corregirlo. Los dos moldes basicos: It + be + X + that/who... (it-cleft) y What + oracion + be + X (wh-cleft o pseudo-cleft), donde X es la informacion que quieres resaltar.

sections.heading: 1 - It-clefts
sections.body:
Estructura: It + be + [elemento destacado] + that / who + resto.

Sirve para poner el foco (y a menudo contrastar) en un sujeto, objeto, complemento o circunstancial. Personas: who o that; lugar / tiempo: that (no where / when). be concuerda con it (normalmente is / was). El verbo principal no se focaliza con un it-cleft.
examples: It was John who broke the window.
It was in Paris that they met.
It wasn't me who told her.
It is only now that I understand.

sections.heading: 2 - Wh-clefts (pseudo-clefts)
sections.body:
Estructura: What + [oracion] + be + [foco]. El foco (informacion nueva) va al final.

Muy util para "preparar el terreno" antes de dar el dato importante. be concuerda con el foco: What I need is a rest / What I need are new shoes.
examples: What I need is a holiday.
What surprised me was his reaction.
What matters is the result, not the effort.
What happened was that the deal fell through.

sections.heading: 3 - All-clefts
sections.body: Como un wh-cleft pero con All (that) en lugar de What. Anade el matiz de "solo esto y nada mas". El that es opcional.
examples: All I want is a coffee.
All you have to do is ask.
All she said was "sorry".
All we can do is wait.

sections.heading: 4 - The reason / the thing / the place ... is ...
sections.body: Variantes del wh-cleft con un sustantivo (the reason, the thing, the person, the place, the day, the moment) + clausula de relativo + be + foco.
examples: The reason (why) I called is to invite you.
The thing that annoys me is the noise.
The place where we met was a small cafe.
The one thing you mustn't do is panic.

sections.heading: 5 - Wh-clefts invertidos
sections.body: Se le da la vuelta al wh-cleft: [foco] + be + what-clause. Muy comun al senalar algo o resumir.
examples: A holiday is what we all need.
That is what I meant.
Trust is what a team is built on.
Results are what count, not promises.

sections.heading: 6 - Clefts que enfatizan la accion
sections.body:
Para destacar lo que alguien hizo: What + sujeto + do/does/did + be + (to) infinitivo. El to es opcional.

Tambien: All he did was + (to) infinitivo.
examples: What he did was (to) ignore the warning.
What we need to do is act now.
All they did was laugh.
What I'll do is call the police.

sections.heading: 7 - Para que sirven y su registro
sections.body:
Los clefts sirven para focalizar un elemento, contrastar o corregir (It was Ana, not Sara, who called) e introducir informacion nueva de forma ordenada.

It-clefts: tipicos de la escritura y el habla formal. Wh-clefts: comunes en habla y escritura para conducir al oyente hacia el punto clave. Abusar de ellos hace el texto pesado.
examples: It was Ana, not Sara, who called. (correccion)
What's important is that everyone is safe. (enmarca el punto clave)
It is with great sadness that we announce... (tono ceremonial)

sections.heading: 8 - Transformar a oracion escindida
sections.body:
Elige el elemento que quieres destacar:

  • Nombre / circunstancia → It + be + X + that/who...
  • Lo que se necesita / quiere / importa → What + oracion + be + X
  • Una accion → What + sujeto + did + be + (to) infinitivo

Cualquier wh-cleft se puede invertir (X is what...). Errores: where/when en it-clefts (usa that); it de mas en wh-clefts.
examples: Ana wrote the report. → It was Ana who wrote the report.
I need a break. → What I need is a break.
She resigned. → What she did was resign.

mistakes: NO: It was in the park where we met. -> SI: It was in the park that we met.
NO: It was yesterday when I saw her. -> SI: It was yesterday that I saw her.
NO: What I want it is a holiday. -> SI: What I want is a holiday.
NO: That I want is peace. -> SI: What I want is peace.
NO: What he did was resigned. -> SI: What he did was (to) resign.
NO: It were the workers who complained. -> SI: It was the workers who complained.
NO: It is his courage what I admire. -> SI: It is his courage that I admire.
